density.few-title: Not enough analyses for the density curve
density.few-description: The curve needs at least {{min}} analyses, and the period has {{amount}}. The histogram and the summary still apply.
density.same-title: Not enough analyses with different values for the curve
density.same-description: The {{amount}} of the period have the same value, and the curve needs different values to show the shape of the distribution.
density.caption: The area under the curve adds up to 1: the higher the curve in a stretch, the more analyses concentrate there. The dashed line marks the median.

boxplot.caption: Each box goes from Q1 to Q3, with the median mark, and the whiskers go up to the last value within the limits. The hollow circles are the outliers.
boxplot.metric-note: The metrics of {{name}} have their own scale and do not fit the 0 to 1 axis. Choose the Metric level to see the distribution of each one.

scatter.caption: Each point is an analysis, on the date it was made. The light band goes from Q1 to Q3, where the middle 50% of the analyses are, and the dashed line marks the median.

summary-card.note: The IQR is the distance between Q3 and Q1, where the middle 50% of the analyses are. Outliers are the analyses outside the limits: below Q1 − 1,5 × IQR or above Q3 + 1,5 × IQR. Standard deviation and variance measure how far the analyses are from the mean and, being sample statistics, need at least 2 analyses.
summary-card.skewness-default: Positive skewness: the long tail is on the right (isolated high values). Negative: on the left (isolated low values).
